text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - The UK stock market set record highs but failed to live up to its early promise and retreated back to the key 4,000 level by the close as investors played safe ahead of Friday's key U.S. employment data. The FTSE 100 index, which had set a record 4,024.3 points on the back of strong gilts prices and an influx of cash, turned tail as futures prices declined and closed the day at 4,000 points down 15.1 points.

FRANKFURT - The German share market was closed on Thursday for a national holiday. Regular trading will resume on Friday. The 30-share DAX index ended IBIS dealings on Wednesday up 30.95 points at 2,685.29, while the DAX ended bourse trade up 20.77 points at 2,676.50.

PARIS - French stocks finished slightly lower as the bourse paused for breath after the previous day's strong gains, bonds were flat, and disappointment with half-year results at some companies weighed on the bourse's CAC-40 index, which closed down 5.75 points or 0.27 percent at 2,136.09.

ZURICH - Swiss shares recovered from intra-day lows to end firmer, closing above an important resistance mark around 3,760/70 points on the Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 8.02 points or 0.33 percent to 2,415.18.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks settled lower, forefeiting the gains they made earlier when they were inspired by the Dow's rise to a record high overnight, brokers said activity was quiet across the board and that profit-taking eroded the Nikkei average. The 225-issue Nikkei average ended down 167.10 points or 0.78 percent at 21,331.50.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng index powered through the 12,000 point level, closing above that mark for the first time since February 1994, buoyed by local fundamentals and record highs in overseas markets. The Hang Seng closed up 62.68 points at 12,014.56.
SYDNEY - Australian shares ended barely firmer as profit-takers stepped in after the market touched a year high on early Dow-inspired gains. The All Ordinaries index closed 0.3 points up at 2,314.9.

JOHANNESBURG - Rebelling against a weak rand industrial and all-shares held their heads above opening levels to end moderately higher and extend the previous day's climb, reinforced by Wednesday's strong march and Wall Street's second record close in a row, shares took courage from the U.S. market's steady open and a stolid local futures market. The Overall index ended up 17.4 points at 7,014.5, Industrials were up 21.9 points to 8,226.1 and Golds were off 9.3 points to 1,722.5.
